items.prompt: A friend shows you a logo they designed and asks your opinion. Which reply fits best?
options: The colours feel a bit busy and the text could be easier to read.
The colours clash and the text is hard to read. Change both before printing.
items.target: The colours clash and the text is hard to read. Change both before printing.

items.prompt: A coworker asks whether their presentation went well. Which reply fits best?
options: It ran long and the middle section lost the room. Cut ten minutes.
It ran a little long and the middle felt slower for the room.
items.target: It ran long and the middle section lost the room. Cut ten minutes.

items.prompt: Your neighbour asks whether their dog's barking bothers you. Which reply fits best?
options: A little, honestly; it tends to bark around six and we hear it.
Yes. It barks every morning at six and wakes the baby up.
items.target: Yes. It barks every morning at six and wakes the baby up.

items.prompt: A student asks whether their essay is ready to submit. Which reply fits best?
options: Almost; the argument could be firmer and the conclusion echoes the introduction.
No. The argument is weak and the conclusion just repeats the introduction.
items.target: No. The argument is weak and the conclusion just repeats the introduction.

items.prompt: A friend asks whether they should text their ex tonight. Which advice fits best?
options: Don't. They ended it twice, and you'll feel worse by tomorrow morning.
I'd hold off; they ended it twice, and you may feel worse.
items.target: Don't. They ended it twice, and you'll feel worse by tomorrow morning.

items.prompt: A diner asks the waiter whether the fish is fresh today. Which reply fits best?
options: It's from Tuesday. Order the chicken instead; it came in today.
It arrived Tuesday; the chicken might be a fresher choice tonight.
items.target: It's from Tuesday. Order the chicken instead; it came in today.

items.prompt: A manager is writing to an applicant who didn't get the job. Which message fits best?
options: You didn't get the role. Another candidate had more management experience.
We've gone with another candidate whose experience was a closer match.
items.target: You didn't get the role. Another candidate had more management experience.

items.prompt: Your partner asks how their new haircut looks. Which reply fits best?
options: It's quite short at the back; I think I liked the longer style.
It's too short at the back. I preferred it the old way.
items.target: It's too short at the back. I preferred it the old way.

items.prompt: A tenant asks the landlord whether the rent will go up this year. Which reply fits best?
options: I'm afraid so, by about eighty pounds a month from June.
Yes, by eighty pounds a month, starting the first of June.
items.target: Yes, by eighty pounds a month, starting the first of June.

items.prompt: A colleague asks for comments on an email they drafted to a client. Which comment fits best?
options: It's too long. Cut the first two paragraphs and get to the point faster.
It might be shorter; dropping the first two paragraphs would bring the point forward.
items.target: It's too long. Cut the first two paragraphs and get to the point faster.

items.prompt: A friend asks whether they can sing at your wedding. Which reply fits best?
options: That's kind, but we've booked a singer and the schedule is full.
No. We've already booked a singer, and the schedule is full anyway.
items.target: No. We've already booked a singer, and the schedule is full anyway.

items.prompt: A customer asks a mechanic whether their tyres are safe. Which reply fits best?
options: No. The front two are bald and you shouldn't drive on them at all.
The front two are quite worn; I'd replace them before driving much more.
items.target: No. The front two are bald and you shouldn't drive on them at all.

items.prompt: A teammate asks why their pull request hasn't been approved. Which reply fits best?
options: A couple of login tests fail, and the naming could be more consistent.
It breaks the login tests and the naming is inconsistent. Fix both.
items.target: It breaks the login tests and the naming is inconsistent. Fix both.

items.prompt: A relative asks whether you enjoyed the holiday dinner they cooked. Which reply fits best?
options: The turkey was dry and overcooked, but the potatoes were excellent.
The potatoes were excellent; the turkey was a touch dry.
items.target: The turkey was dry and overcooked, but the potatoes were excellent.

items.prompt: A runner asks their coach whether they're ready for a marathon. Which reply fits best?
options: Not yet. Your long runs stop at twelve miles; you need twenty.
Getting there; your long runs only reach twelve miles so far.
items.target: Not yet. Your long runs stop at twelve miles; you need twenty.

items.prompt: A friend asks whether their business idea will make money. Which reply fits best?
options: It may be tough; three shops on your street already sell it.
Probably not. Three shops on your street already sell the same thing.
items.target: Probably not. Three shops on your street already sell the same thing.

items.prompt: A reader asks a librarian whether they can keep a book another month. Which reply fits best?
options: No, it's reserved by someone else. Bring it back by Friday.
Someone else has reserved it, so could you return it Friday?
items.target: No, it's reserved by someone else. Bring it back by Friday.

items.prompt: A homeowner asks a builder whether the extension can be done by summer. Which reply fits best?
options: No. The permits alone take four months, so it's autumn.
Unlikely, I'm afraid; the permits alone take around four months.
items.target: No. The permits alone take four months, so it's autumn.

items.prompt: A friend asks how their date went, since you were at the next table. Which reply fits best?
options: You did most of the talking, and she seemed a little less engaged.
You talked about yourself the entire time and she looked bored by dessert.
items.target: You talked about yourself the entire time and she looked bored by dessert.

items.prompt: A patient asks the dentist how their teeth look. Which reply fits best?
options: You have two cavities. Floss every day or you'll get more.
There are two small cavities; daily flossing would help prevent more.
items.target: You have two cavities. Floss every day or you'll get more.

items.prompt: A parent asks a swimming instructor whether their child can move up a class. Which reply fits best?
options: Not just yet; she's still working on swimming a full length.
No. She still can't swim a full length without stopping to rest.
items.target: No. She still can't swim a full length without stopping to rest.

items.prompt: A volunteer asks why they weren't picked to lead the fundraiser. Which reply fits best?
options: You missed two planning meetings, so we chose someone else to lead.
We went with someone who made all the planning meetings this time.
items.target: You missed two planning meetings, so we chose someone else to lead.

items.prompt: A friend asks what you think of the apartment they just rented. Which reply fits best?
options: It's cosy, though a bit dark, and the rent seems high.
It's dark and small, and the rent is too high for it.
items.target: It's dark and small, and the rent is too high for it.

items.prompt: A writer asks an editor whether their article can run tomorrow. Which reply fits best?
options: Not quite yet; two quotes need sources and the lead needs another look.
No. Two quotes aren't sourced and the lead is wrong. Fix them first.
items.target: No. Two quotes aren't sourced and the lead is wrong. Fix them first.

items.prompt: A colleague asks whether you minded them presenting your analysis in the meeting. Which reply fits best?
options: Yes, I did. That analysis was mine and you didn't mention my name.
It did bother me a little; the analysis was mine and I wasn't mentioned.
items.target: Yes, I did. That analysis was mine and you didn't mention my name.

items.prompt: A tourist asks a local whether a famous restaurant is worth visiting. Which reply fits best?
options: No. It's overpriced, the food is ordinary, and service is slow.
Maybe not; it's pricey, the food is plain, and service is slow.
items.target: No. It's overpriced, the food is ordinary, and service is slow.

items.prompt: A friend asks you to look over their CV. Which comment fits best?
options: There are two typos on page one, and the summary says nothing.
There are two small typos on page one; the summary could say more.
items.target: There are two typos on page one, and the summary says nothing.

items.prompt: A client asks a designer why the website project is late. Which reply fits best?
options: The brief changed a few times, which added about six weeks.
You changed the brief three times, and that added six weeks.
items.target: You changed the brief three times, and that added six weeks.

items.prompt: A gym member asks a trainer about their squat form. Which reply fits best?
options: Your knees drift inward and your back rounds; a lighter weight might help.
Your knees cave in and your back rounds. Take weight off the bar.
items.target: Your knees cave in and your back rounds. Take weight off the bar.

items.prompt: A friend asks whether they should adopt a second cat. Which advice fits best?
options: No. Your flat is small and the first cat already scratches everything.
Maybe wait; your flat is small and the first cat already scratches a lot.
items.target: No. Your flat is small and the first cat already scratches everything.

items.prompt: A roommate asks whether their music is too loud at night. Which reply fits best?
options: A bit, yes; I can hear it through the wall after midnight.
Yes. I can hear every word through the wall after midnight.
items.target: Yes. I can hear every word through the wall after midnight.

items.prompt: A bride asks a tailor whether her dress can be altered within a week. Which reply fits best?
options: No. That much beading takes three weeks at the very least.
That's tight; beading like this usually takes about three weeks.
items.target: No. That much beading takes three weeks at the very least.

items.prompt: A hiker asks a ranger whether the summit trail is open today. Which reply fits best?
options: It's closed today; there's ice above the ridge and it's been slippery.
It's closed. There's ice above the ridge and people have fallen.
items.target: It's closed. There's ice above the ridge and people have fallen.

items.prompt: Your nephew asks whether his band could play at your company party. Which reply fits best?
options: No. The crowd wants covers people know, and your songs are all originals.
Probably not this time; the crowd wants familiar covers, and your set is originals.
items.target: No. The crowd wants covers people know, and your songs are all originals.

items.prompt: A friend asks why you left their party early. Which reply fits best?
options: I didn't know anyone, and the music was too loud to talk over.
I didn't know many people, and it was hard to talk over the music.
items.target: I didn't know anyone, and the music was too loud to talk over.

items.prompt: An employee asks why their raise was smaller than expected. Which reply fits best?
options: Two quarters came in under target, which kept the raise more modest.
You missed your targets in two quarters, so the raise is smaller.
items.target: You missed your targets in two quarters, so the raise is smaller.

items.prompt: A friend who loves cooking asks what you think of their new curry. Which reply fits best?
options: It's too sweet and the spices are flat. Add some acid and more chilli.
It leans sweet and the spices feel quiet; acid and chilli might lift it.
items.target: It's too sweet and the spices are flat. Add some acid and more chilli.

items.prompt: A parent asks a teacher how their daughter's reading is going. Which reply fits best?
options: She reads a full year below her age and avoids books during class.
She's reading a little behind her age and is reluctant with books in class.
items.target: She reads a full year below her age and avoids books during class.

items.prompt: An owner asks the vet whether their old dog will recover. Which reply fits best?
options: I'm afraid not; the tumour has spread and his time is short.
No, he won't. The tumour has spread and he has weeks left.
items.target: No, he won't. The tumour has spread and he has weeks left.

items.prompt: A friend asks whether they should quit their job to travel for a year. Which advice fits best?
options: Not without savings. You'd come back broke and jobless in a year.
Build some savings first, or coming back could be very hard.
items.target: Not without savings. You'd come back broke and jobless in a year.

items.prompt: A coworker asks you to cover their shift again this weekend. Which reply fits best?
options: Not this time; I've done three shifts this month and I'm tired.
No. I've already covered three shifts this month and I'm exhausted.
items.target: No. I've already covered three shifts this month and I'm exhausted.

items.prompt: A customer asks a salesperson whether the cheaper laptop will do for video editing. Which reply fits best?
options: No. It's too slow for video editing, so buy the more expensive one.
For video editing it may feel slow; the other suits you better.
items.target: No. It's too slow for video editing, so buy the more expensive one.

items.prompt: A best man asks for your thoughts on his wedding speech draft. Which reply fits best?
options: It runs a bit long, and the jokes about the ex may not land.
It's too long and the jokes about the ex will offend his family.
items.target: It's too long and the jokes about the ex will offend his family.

items.prompt: A fan asks what you think of their football team's chances this season. Which reply fits best?
options: Mid-table seems likely; the defence is getting on a bit.
They'll finish mid-table at best. The defence is too old.
items.target: They'll finish mid-table at best. The defence is too old.

items.prompt: A host asks a guest whether the living room is warm enough. Which reply fits best?
options: No, it's cold in here. Can you turn the heating up?
It's a little chilly; would you mind turning the heating up?
items.target: No, it's cold in here. Can you turn the heating up?

items.prompt: A researcher asks a colleague to read their grant proposal. Which comment fits best?
options: The aims are vague and the budget doesn't add up. Redo both.
The aims could be sharper and the budget needs another check.
items.target: The aims are vague and the budget doesn't add up. Redo both.

items.prompt: A friend asks what you think of the wedding venue she has chosen. Which reply fits best?
options: It's too far out. Half the guests will need hotels.
It's quite far out, so many guests may need hotels.
items.target: It's too far out. Half the guests will need hotels.

items.prompt: A teenager asks whether they can borrow the family car this weekend. Which reply fits best?
options: Not this weekend; the scratch from last time still needs sorting.
No. You scratched it last time and haven't paid for it.
items.target: No. You scratched it last time and haven't paid for it.

items.prompt: A neighbour asks what you think of the new hedge they planted. Which reply fits best?
options: It shades our garden in the afternoon; could it be kept lower?
It blocks our light in the afternoon. Please keep it lower.
items.target: It blocks our light in the afternoon. Please keep it lower.

items.prompt: A friend asks why you didn't like the film they recommended. Which reply fits best?
options: The plot made no sense and it was an hour too long.
I lost the thread of the plot, and it felt overlong.
items.target: The plot made no sense and it was an hour too long.

items.prompt: A new manager asks how their first week leading the team went. Which reply fits best?
options: A couple of people mentioned feeling cut off in meetings.
Two people complained that you interrupt them in every meeting.
items.target: Two people complained that you interrupt them in every meeting.

items.prompt: A customer asks a baker for a three-tier cake by tomorrow. Which reply fits best?
options: No. Three tiers need two days. I can do one tier.
Three tiers usually need two days, but one tier is possible.
items.target: No. Three tiers need two days. I can do one tier.

items.prompt: A friend asks whether their poem is good enough for a competition. Which reply fits best?
options: Nearly; the ending could be stronger and some rhymes feel forced.
Not yet. The ending is weak and the rhymes feel forced.
items.target: Not yet. The ending is weak and the rhymes feel forced.

items.prompt: A traveller asks a gate agent whether they will make their connecting flight. Which reply fits best?
options: No. Your flight is delayed two hours and the connection leaves in one.
It's unlikely; the delay is two hours and the connection leaves in one.
items.target: No. Your flight is delayed two hours and the connection leaves in one.

items.prompt: An actor asks the director for notes after rehearsal. Which note fits best?
options: You rushed your lines and nobody in the back could hear you.
Your lines came a little fast, and the back rows struggled to hear.
items.target: You rushed your lines and nobody in the back could hear you.

items.prompt: A homeowner asks a plumber whether the old boiler can be repaired. Which reply fits best?
options: It's twenty years old, so replacing it before winter would be wise.
No. It's twenty years old and parts are gone. Replace it before winter.
items.target: No. It's twenty years old and parts are gone. Replace it before winter.

items.prompt: A neighbour asks whether you'll join the street's residents' committee. Which reply fits best?
options: No. I don't have the time and I don't enjoy committee meetings.
I'll pass; my time is tight and meetings aren't my thing.
items.target: No. I don't have the time and I don't enjoy committee meetings.

items.prompt: Your sister asks whether her new boyfriend made a good impression at dinner. Which reply fits best?
options: Not really. He was rude to the waiter and checked his phone constantly.
Mixed, honestly; he was short with the waiter and often on his phone.
items.target: Not really. He was rude to the waiter and checked his phone constantly.

items.prompt: A founder asks an investor for feedback after a pitch. Which reply fits best?
options: The projections feel optimistic, so we'll pass at this stage.
Your numbers are unrealistic and we won't invest at this stage.
items.target: Your numbers are unrealistic and we won't invest at this stage.

items.prompt: A cyclist asks a bike shop whether their frame is safe after a crash. Which reply fits best?
options: It's cracked. Don't ride it again; the frame could snap on you.
There's a crack, so I'd stop riding it; it could fail.
items.target: It's cracked. Don't ride it again; the frame could snap on you.
